record.original_question: What is the lowest degree of a polynomial mapping P : R2 → R2 for which the (real) Jacobian conjecture fails, i.e. the Jacobian of P never vanishes while p fails to be invertible.

evidence.quote: Problem 9.2.2 (New) What is the lowest degree of a polynomial mapping P : R2 → R2 for which the (real) Jacobian conjecture fails, i.e. the Jacobian of P never vanishes while p fails to be invertible. 9.3 Proper correspondences

artifact.self_contained_problem: Determine the smallest positive integer d with the following property: there exists a polynomial map P = (p, q) : R^2 → R^2, with p, q ∈ R[x, y] and max(deg p, deg q) = d (equivalently, total degree d), such that the Jacobian determinant det(DP)(x, y) = ∂p/∂x · ∂q/∂y − ∂p/∂y · ∂q/∂x is nowhere zero on R^2, yet the map P fails to be injective (and hence is not a global diffeomorphism of R^2 onto its image). In other words, find the lowest degree at which the real Jacobian conjecture in dimension two can fail.
artifact.status_search_result: Pinchuk gave the first counterexamples to the strong real Jacobian conjecture (with component degrees on the order of 10 and 25, total degree ~35). Subsequent work has lowered the known degrees of counterexamples (e.g., constructions with components of degrees 10 and 15, and counterexamples built from certain degree-9 auxiliary polynomials), but the exact minimum degree at which the real Jacobian conjecture in R^2 fails has not been determined. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: Provides a non-injective local polynomial diffeomorphism with components of degrees 10 and 15, lower than the previously known 10 and 25.
status_evidence.claim: Lower-degree counterexamples have been constructed, indicating the minimum degree question is active and unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Very degenerate polynomial submersions and counterexamples to the real Jacobian conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs new counterexamples to the real Jacobian conjecture using degree-9 auxiliary polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Recent research continues to lower degrees of known counterexamples, with the optimal degree still unknown.
